1.1: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by God's will, and Timothy our brother,
1.2: To the saints and faithful brothers and sisters in Christ who are in Colossae: Grace and peace to y'all from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1.3: We thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, and we're always praying for y'all,
1.4: Since we heard about your faith in Christ Jesus and your love for all the saints,
1.5: Because of the hope laid up for y'all in heaven, the hope you heard about before in the word of truth, the gospel,
1.6: Which has come to you, just like it has to the whole world, and it's bearing fruit, just like it's been doing among you since the day you heard and understood the grace of God in truth.
1.7: Just like you learned from Epaphras, our dear fellow servant, who's a faithful minister of Christ on your behalf,
1.8: Who also told us about your love in the Spirit.
1.9: For this reason, since the day we heard it, we don't stop praying for you, and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of His will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;
1.10: So that you may walk worthy of the Lord, fully pleasing Him, bearing fruit in every good work, and growing in the knowledge of God;
1.11: Strengthened with all might, according to His glorious power, for all patience and long-suffering with joy;
1.12: Giving thanks to the Father, who qualified us to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light.
1.13: He has delivered us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of His love,
1.14: In whom we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins.
1.15: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation.
1.16: For by Him, all things were created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones, dominions, principalities, or powers. All things were created through Him and for Him.
1.17: And He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.
1.18: And He is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that in everything He may have the preeminence.
1.19: It pleased the Father that in Him all the fullness should dwell,
1.20: And by Him, to reconcile all things to Himself—whether things on earth or things in heaven—making peace through the blood of His cross.
1.21: And y'all, who once were alienated and enemies in your minds by wicked works, He has now reconciled
1.22: In the body of His flesh through death, to present y'all holy, blameless, and above reproach in His sight—
1.23: If indeed you continue in the faith, grounded and steadfast, and aren't moved away from the hope of the gospel you heard, the gospel which was preached to every creature under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a minister.
1.24: Now I rejoice in my sufferings for y'all, and I'm filling up in my flesh what's lacking in the afflictions of Christ, for the sake of His body, which is the church,
1.25: Of which I became a minister according to the stewardship from God that was given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God,
1.26: The mystery that's been hidden for ages and generations, but now has been revealed to His saints.
1.27: To them, God willed to make known what are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles: which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.
1.28: Him we preach, warning every person and teaching everyone in all wisdom, so that we may present every person perfect in Christ Jesus.
1.29: For this purpose, I labor, striving according to His working, which works in me mightily.

2.1: Look, I need y'all to understand how much I'm grinding for you and the folks in Laodicea, and all the ones who ain't even met me in person,
2.2: So their hearts get encouraged, being tied up together in love, and getting the full assurance of understanding, the knowledge of the mystery of God, the Father, and Christ,
2.3: In Him, all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.
2.4: I'm saying all this so nobody can come at you with smooth talk and trick you with fancy words.
2.5: Even though I'm not there physically, I'm with you in spirit, and I'm happy to see y'all holding it down with good order and staying strong in your faith in Christ.
2.6: So, since you've already received Christ Jesus as Lord, walk in Him,
2.7: Rooted and built up in Him, and solid in the faith like you were taught, overflowing with thanksgiving.
2.8: Watch out! Don't let nobody cheat you with all that philosophy and empty lies, following the traditions of men, following the basic principles of the world, and not Christ.
2.9: For in Him, the fullness of God lives bodily,
2.10: And you are complete in Him, who is the head of all power and authority.
2.11: In Him, you got the real circumcision, not by human hands, but by putting off the body of sin—through the circumcision of Christ,
2.12: You were buried with Him in baptism, and through faith in God, who raised Him from the dead, you were raised with Him,
2.13: And though you were dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, He made you alive with Him, forgiving all your sins,
2.14: He wiped out the debt we owed with all the rules that were against us—He took it outta the way and nailed it to the cross.
2.15: He disarmed the powers and authorities, made a public show of them, and triumphed over them on the cross.
2.16: So don't let anyone judge you on what you eat or drink, or if you celebrate a festival, a new moon, or sabbaths,
2.17: These things were just a shadow of what's to come, but the reality is in Christ.
2.18: Don't let anyone cheat you outta your reward, acting all humble and worshiping angels, getting deep into things they never even seen, being all puffed up in their fleshly mind,
2.19: And not holding on to the Head, from whom the whole body—nourished and connected by joints and ligaments—grows with the increase that comes from God.
2.20: If you died with Christ and left the basic rules of this world behind, why are you still acting like you gotta follow man-made rules,
2.21: "Don't touch this, don't taste that, don't handle this,"
2.22: All that stuff is temporary, and it's based on human commandments and teachings.
2.23: These rules might seem wise with all their self-imposed religion, fake humility, and neglect of the body, but they don't do anything to stop the flesh from indulging.

3.1: So, if you were raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, sittin' at God's right hand,
3.2: Set your mind on things above, not on stuff down here.
3.3: You died to your old life, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
3.4: When Christ, who is our life, shows up, you gon' show up with Him in glory.
3.5: So, put to death the stuff that's all about this earth: fornication, uncleanness, passion, evil desires, and greed, which is idolatry.
3.6: 'Cause of all this mess, the wrath of God is coming for the disobedient,
3.7: And y'all used to walk in these ways when you was living like that.
3.8: But now, y'all need to get rid of all of this: anger, wrath, malice, blasphemy, and filthy language outta your mouth.
3.9: Don't be out here lying to each other, since you've put off the old self with its ways,
3.10: And put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge, according to the image of the One who created it,
3.11: Here's the real deal: There ain't no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free—Christ is all, and He's in all of us.
3.12: So, as God's chosen people, holy and loved, put on tender mercy, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience,
3.13: Bear with each other, and forgive each other. If anyone has a complaint, forgive them just like Christ forgave you.
3.14: But above everything, put on love, that's the glue that holds everything together.
3.15: Let God's peace rule in your heart, since you were called to peace in one body, and be thankful.
3.16: Let the word of Christ live richly in you, teaching and encouraging each other with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.
3.17: And whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.
3.18: Wives, submit to your husbands, as it's fitting in the Lord.
3.19: Husbands, love your wives and don't be bitter toward them.
3.20: Children, obey your parents in everything, 'cause that pleases the Lord.
3.21: Fathers, don't provoke your kids, or they'll get discouraged.
3.22: Bondservants, obey your masters in everything, not just when they're watching, trying to please people, but with a sincere heart, fearing God.
3.23: Whatever you do, do it with all your heart, as if you're doing it for the Lord, not for men,
3.24: Knowing that from the Lord, you will receive the reward of the inheritance; you're serving the Lord Christ.
3.25: But anyone who does wrong is gonna get what they deserve, and God don't show no partiality.

4.1: Masters, give your bondservants what's just and fair, knowing that you got a Master in heaven too.
4.2: Keep on praying earnestly, always alert in prayer with thanksgiving;
4.3: Meanwhile, pray for us too, that God would open a door for us to spread the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I'm locked up in chains,
4.4: So I can make it clear, like I should.
4.5: Walk in wisdom toward those who ain't saved, making the most of your time,
4.6: Let your speech always be full of grace, with just the right amount of spice, so you'll know how to answer everyone.
4.7: Tychicus, my beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow servant in the Lord, will fill you in on everything about me.
4.8: I'm sending him to you for this very reason, so he can get the scoop on how you're doing and bring some comfort to your hearts,
4.9: With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who's one of y'all. They gon' tell you everything going down over here.
4.10: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, says "what's up," along with Mark, Barnabas' cousin (about whom you got the instructions: if he comes through, show him love),
4.11: And Jesus, who's called Justus. These are the only fellow workers I got for the kingdom who are from the circumcision, and they've been a comfort to me.
4.12: Epaphras, who's one of y'all, a bondservant of Christ, sends his greetings, always praying hard for y'all, that you stand strong and complete in God's will.
4.13: I can vouch for him—he's got mad love for y'all, and for the people in Laodicea and Hierapolis.
4.14: Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas send their greetings.
4.15: Greet the believers in Laodicea, and Nymphas, and the church in his house.
4.16: When you read this letter, make sure you share it with the church in Laodicea, and read the letter from them too.
4.17: And tell Archippus: "Pay attention to the ministry you received from the Lord, and make sure you finish it."
4.18: This greeting is from me, Paul, with my own hand. Don't forget my chains. Grace be with you. Amen.
